llm.summary: The skill is mostly purpose-aligned, but it needs Review because it can broadly activate, write and serve repo reports without a consent gate, and its generated HTML report has a script-injection risk from untrusted repo data.

dimensions.detail: Writing .slop-check files and slop-report.html is proportionate to the reporting purpose, and the server binds to 127.0.0.1, but the generated report embeds JSON directly inside an inline script without escaping script-ending sequences, which can let malicious repo-controlled data execute JavaScript when the report is opened.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No dependency installation, remote payload fetch, package manager hook, or privileged install step was found. The bundled scripts are local Node 18+ scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger description includes generic requests such as audit, report card, code quality score, and code smells, so the skill could run repo-wide scanning, file creation, and serving when the user intended a lighter review. The instructions do not require explicit consent before those side effects.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates persistent report artifacts in the target repo and starts a local server that runs until stopped, but I found no OS-level persistence, credential access, privilege escalation, or external network exfiltration behavior.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The core behavior coherently matches a codebase grading/reporting skill: it scans local code, computes metrics, produces findings, and generates fix-it prompts. The capability is broad because it analyzes an entire repository and may use multiple reviewer agents, but that is disclosed in the skill instructions.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with repo-wide local code analysis, generated files under .slop-check plus slop-report.html, and a temporary localhost report server. Avoid running it on untrusted repositories until the report data embedding is fixed, or run it in a disposable checkout and open the report cautiously. Stop the local server when finished and review generated artifacts before sharing them.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted as a scoping concern: the trigger text is broader than explicit slop-check or repo-grading intent and can cause high-effort repo scanning and report generation on ordinary review requests.
[P2] expected: Downgraded: the flagged HTML comment describes how the bundled template is built and does not contain an instruction to hijack the evaluating agent or the user's agent.
[SQP-2] expected: Partly accepted: report file creation and localhost serving are expected for this skill, but the lack of an explicit user consent or no-server mode is a real Review concern.
[SDI-2] expected: Downgraded: slop-map.json is disclosed in SKILL.md and supports the advertised fix-it prompts by preserving import graph context for later repairs; it is additional output but not purpose-mismatched.
[SQP-2] expected: Partly accepted for REPORT-SCHEMA.md: writing report-data.json and running build-report.mjs are normal report-generation steps, but they are state-changing actions without a required confirmation gate.
[SDI-4] expected: Downgraded: the token-spending wording is imprecise, but it does not create hidden authority or deceptive runtime behavior.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted as a substantive implementation risk: build-report.mjs injects JSON.stringify output directly into an inline script in report-template.html, so untrusted values containing a script terminator can break out before later DOM escaping runs.
